text:
alex: Quick follow-up on the authn/authz RFC — we need a concrete pattern for API key scoping and service-to-service auth before we start the api_keys table migration.

morgan: Agreed. Two main constraints: 1) minimal token size for low-bandwidth clients, 2) clear principal/subject for audit logs. We should avoid per-route permissions on keys (too chatty) and use org/project scoping + role bindings.

sarah-m: +1. Proposal: API keys carry claims: org_id, project_id (optional), and a role_id which maps to a set of permissions. Roles are namespaced to orgs. That lets us evaluate RBAC server-side without exploding key permutations.

alex: Sounds reasonable. How do we handle service auth (k8s pods -> backend)? Do we issue short-lived JWTs or mint long-lived service tokens? Tradeoffs: short-lived JWTs = better security, needs token service; long-lived = simpler for infra.

morgan: I prefer short-lived JWTs with refresh via a mint endpoint (internal only). Pattern: workloads authenticate with a mTLS-validated client cert to the mint service, get a signed JWT with aud=service and exp=+15m, include org_id claim. Then services validate signature + aud + scope.

jim: Operational note: signature verification cost at high QPS. We should cache public keys and validate locally. Also add a token-introspection fallback for older services during migration.

sarah-m: For API keys we can't require mTLS. Keep them as opaque IDs in DB that map to metadata (org, project, role). We'll return an API-key header that the proxy expands into internal JWT for downstream services (proxy does introspect and mint short internal JWT).

alex: So flow summary: external API key -> proxy (expand DB lookup) -> proxy mints short-lived internal JWT for downstream calls. For service-to-service, pods use mTLS -> mint service JWT. Both JWT shapes similar so apps validate same codepath.

morgan: Example JWT claims we discussed:

```
{
  "iss": "auth.redwood.internal",
  "sub": "svc-12345",     // service principal or api-key-id
  "org": "org_987",
  "proj": "proj_abc",     // optional
  "role": "read-only",
  "aud": "inference-service",
  "exp": 1710000000
}
```

sarah-m: Important: role should NOT be an allowlist of routes; keep it coarse (e.g., read, write, admin). Route-level checks stay in policy layer with feature flags for fine-grained controls.

jim: DB changes: add columns to api_keys: org_id, project_id nullable, role_id, owner_user, rotated_at. We'll also add a `kind` enum: external_api_key | service_token to differentiate.

alex: Backcompat/migration: create a compatibility proxy that responds to old key format. Migration plan: 1) add new columns (no-op), 2) start filling metadata for new keys, 3) opt-in services to validate JWTs, 4) flip proxy to mint JWTs for all external keys, 5) deprecate raw key checks.

infra-bot: deploy: feature_flag created: rollout/api-key-jwt-minting. Can toggle per-cluster.

morgan: One more: audit logs must record both the original external principal (api-key-id or svc-id) and the minted JWT id to trace causality. Keep logs structured: actor_id, original_type, org, project, action, request_id.

alex: Good. Risks: key leakage if long-lived tokens leak — mitigated by short JWT TTL + rotation. Performance: local key cache + batching validation metrics.

sarah-m: Action items:
- morgan: design mint service API + TTL/rotation policy (due EOD Thu)
- jim: DB migration script + `kind` column (PR by Wed)
- alex: update policy validators to accept new JWT claims (internal PR)
- infra: roll flag to staging and run load test

jim: I'll add a small design doc in eng-security/arch for the mint service and link it here.

alex: Thanks all. If no objections, I'll file the lightweight RFC update and schedule a canary rollout next week. :thumbsup:
